title: Gemini Robotics 2.5 accelerates real-world general dexterity
headline: Google DeepMind releases Gemini Robotics 2.5 with new safety and jailbreak benchmarks
summary: Google DeepMind has introduced Gemini Robotics 2.5, a vision-language-action model designed to improve robot dexterity, reliability, and safety in real-world environments. The release includes new safety features such as real-time physical hazard steerability and the ASIMOV-Jailbreak benchmark to test against adversarial prompts. These developments aim to support the deployment of robots in unstructured settings, including industrial production lines.
why_it_matters: Organisations deploying embodied AI must now account for emerging safety benchmarks and inference-time reasoning guidance to manage physical risks and adversarial threats in human-centric environments.

quotes.text: As robots move into everyday environments, we have improved physical safety steerability and introduced a new benchmark to test against adversarial jailbreaks specific to robotics.

Gemini Robotics 2.5 uses inference-time reasoning guidance to steer around physical hazards in real-time. Much like safety classifiers add a protective layer around Gemini’s responses, this guidance allows the robot to navigate complex environments securely.

classification.significance_reason: The release introduces specific safety benchmarks for embodied AI, setting a new technical standard for managing physical and adversarial risks in robotics.
